chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: RKO theater dressing rooms and Edwina's in Washington
summary: Jackson again describes RKO backstage kitchens and recalls staying and eating at Edwina's near the Howard Theater.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: That's right. Well, you know, in those days, you know, all the RKO theaters had kitchens in the back-stage.
They had kitchens. They had playrooms for the kids if you had kids with you.
Individual shower -- sunken tub and shower in each dressing room.
Adjustable lights. They had a chaise lounge, --
And each dressing room had -- was the name of a state.
And they was beautiful theaters all over the country, --
-- and we played every one of them, you know.
But we had some good places to eat, though.
Do you remember Edwina's in Philadelphia?
Yeah, Edwina's. Oh, yes. I stayed in
Across the street, up the street, from the Howard Theater.
Yeah. Every town had a lady that we relied on, black orchestras and black show people coming in, and they prepared food for us and it was really first class.
And this was the way we survived, right?
